Subject: POC kickoff — aligning stakeholders, goals, and hands-on schedule

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time last week. We'd like to lock the POC kickoff and the hands-on working session (prompt review, routing tests, and a light load trial) so your team can validate latency and routing behavior in a representative flow. Proposed plan attached (redwood_poc_agenda_v1.pdf) and a short prework checklist (nimblebank_prework_list.xlsx).

High-level asks for the kickoff call:
- Introductions: who will own evaluation criteria, security/compliance, and SRE signoff
- Goals: one or two success criteria we can measure by the end of the trial (e.g., per-request P95 < 300ms for 75% of traffic, accuracy threshold on reranking)
- Schedule: 90-minute kickoff + 3-hour hands-on lab within the following 10 business days

Candidate slots (PST):
- Tue Jul 28, 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed Jul 29, 09:00–10:30 or 13:00–14:30
- Thu Jul 30, 11:00–12:30

If none of those work, flag times that do and we'll adjust. Also please tell us who from NimbleBank should attend the hands-on lab (engineer who owns routing, product manager for success criteria, and a security point of contact).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_poc_agenda_v1.pdf, nimblebank_prework_list.xlsx

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the agenda and the clear ask. A couple quick notes from our side:
- Success criteria: product leadership wants throughput and latency visibility, plus one regression threshold on NLU reranking accuracy vs our baseline.
- Attendance: I'll join and bring Sasha (platform lead) and Amir (security/compliance). Tom will coordinate engineers for the hands-on lab.

Availability: Jul 29 09:00–10:30 ET (which is 06:00–07:30 PT) won't work for our East Coast team. The two workable windows for us are:
- Tue Jul 28, 13:00–14:30 ET (10:00–11:30 PT) — OK for all attendees
- Thu Jul 30, 14:00–15:30 ET (11:00–12:30 PT) — backup

Prework: we'll review the agenda and share an internal prompt set that we want to use for routing/load verification. One ask — can you include a short section on how Redwood isolates customer data in Dedicated mode? Amir will want that before the kickoff.

Thanks,
Elena
VP Product — NimbleBank

Quick internal note on lab provisioning and load test constraints:

- For routing tests we need NimbleBank to confirm the routing keys and the fallback policy (e.g., route low-latency queries to variant A, and fallback to B under saturation). If they want to test quantized variants, we’ll also need the expected max sequence lengths for token budget planning.
- I'll prepare a short test-run checklist and a Jupyter snippet to kick off the synthetic traffic. ETA: Monday morning (Jul 27).

Cc'ing Elena so she knows the prep we need from their engineers.
